parts.name: trunk_coconut
sources: The base is swollen, to about 80 cm (Chan and Elevitch, 2006); the model takes 60 cm (an estimate).
A frond is 4.5 to 5.5 m long, the petiole about a quarter of it (Chan and Elevitch, 2006).
30 to 35 fronds in the crown (Chan and Elevitch, 2006; 20 to 40, Palms of New Guinea).
20 to 22 m at 40 years, 20 to 30 m for tall cultivars (Chan and Elevitch, Cocos nucifera, Species Profiles for Pacific Island Agroforestry, 2006): a palm of about 25 years (an estimate).
The leaflets are 50 to 150 cm long, about 100 cm at the middle of the frond, 1.5 to 5 cm wide; 200 to 250 on a frond (Chan and Elevitch, 2006).
The trunk is often curved and usually leans (Plants of the World Online, the floras of Cocos nucifera); the angle is an estimate.

A bunch of about 12 nuts of about 30 by 25 cm under the crown, all the year in the South of Việt Nam (Trần Văn Hâu and Nguyễn Chí Linh, Tạp chí Khoa học ĐH Cần Thơ 17a, 2011: 59 to 72 nuts on a tree each year).
The trunk is 30 to 35 cm across, about 40 cm at the height of the chest, with almost no taper above its base (Chan and Elevitch, 2006).
